biography: Michael 'The Maverick' Mihld didn't come from racing royalty. Born and raised in the dusty backroads of Oklahoma, his first taste of speed was tearing around dirt tracks in a beat-up pickup truck his grandpa had gifted him. He learned the hard way, fixing busted axles under the scorching sun and honing his reflexes on unpredictable terrain. Mihld caught his break at a local county fair race, where he not only won but also impressed a scout from a regional Chevrolet team with his raw talent and fearless driving. The transition to asphalt wasn't easy, but Mihld's grit and refusal to back down quickly earned him a reputation. Now, at 27, he's at the peak of his powers, a force to be reckoned with in the national racing scene, constantly pushing the limits of both his car and his competitors. His aggressive style and relentless pursuit of victory have made him a fan favorite, even if it occasionally ruffles a few feathers in the paddock.
drivingStyle: Mihld's driving style is best described as controlled aggression. He attacks corners with a late-braking technique, often pushing the car right to the edge of grip. Tire management isn't his strongest suit; he prefers to extract maximum performance early in a stint, even if it means sacrificing longevity. Under pressure, Mihld thrives, often pulling off daring overtakes in the closing laps. He's a master of exploiting even the smallest openings, a trait that has earned him both victories and the occasional penalty.

rivalries.reason: A clash of styles. Silva is known for his calculated precision, while Mihld relies on raw aggression. Their contrasting approaches often lead to intense battles on the track.
A fiery rivalry stemming from a controversial incident where Mihld's aggressive maneuver cost Petrova a potential race win. The bad blood has been simmering ever since.
Both drivers are known for their hard-charging, no-holds-barred approach, inevitably leading to frequent on-track clashes and off-track tension.

quirks: Always wears the same worn-out cowboy boots he wore during his first race, regardless of the weather.
Listens to a specific blues track on repeat for an hour before every race to center himself.
Refuses to eat anything green on race days, convinced it brings bad luck.
famousQuote: "Second place is just the first loser. Out here, you either win, or you learn."
careerHighlight: Winning the National Championship at Daytona after starting from the back of the grid due to a pre-race engine change. He charged through the field, making a last-lap pass for the victory.
careerLowPoint: A devastating crash at Indianapolis that sidelined him for three months and raised questions about his overly aggressive driving style.
